micropubr: Publication-Ready Microbiome Visualizations

Source: R/micropubr-package.R
micropubr-package.Rd

micropubr provides a unified, opinionated family of mp_*() functions that turn a phyloseq::phyloseq object into a publication-ready ggplot2 figure with a single call. It applies one consistent design philosophy across the whole microbiome workflow: consistent arguments, colourblind-safe defaults, automatic statistical overlays and reproducible, auto-generated figure captions, while always returning a plain ggplot object you can extend with +.

Core plotting functions

mp_alpha()

Alpha (within-sample) diversity with statistics.

mp_ordination()

Beta diversity / ordination with PERMANOVA.

mp_taxa()

Taxonomic composition (bar, area, heatmap, bubble).

mp_diff()

Differential-abundance result visualisation.

mp_tree()

Annotated phylogenetic trees.

mp_network()

Co-occurrence / correlation networks.

mp_longitudinal()

Time-course and paired-sample plots.

mp_function()

Functional pathway profiles (PICRUSt2/HUMAnN).

Statistical analyses

mp_dispersion()

Multivariate dispersion (PERMDISP) with optional ANOSIM / MRPP / PERMANOVA.

mp_mantel()

Mantel test and correlogram.

mp_varpart()

Variance partitioning among explanatory sets.

mp_prevalence()

Prevalence-abundance and core-microbiome plots.

mp_indicator()

Indicator species analysis.

mp_run_da()

Run a differential-abundance method for mp_diff().

Microbial genomics

mp_coverage()

Genome / contig sequencing-depth tracks.

mp_circos()

Circular (Circos-style) genome plots.

Infrastructure

mp_palette(), the mp_theme_*() family, mp_set_defaults(), mp_combine(), mp_export() and the mp_import_*() helpers. Every plotting function accepts return.data = TRUE to return the tidy data frame behind the plot, and ... to forward arguments to its primary geom.
